text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Liamine Zeroual says the state is committed to fight and wipe out "terrorism".
- Government cabinet approves a draft law on a 380-seat national assembly.
- Fifth anniversary of late president Mohamed Boudiaf's return from exile to take over the ruling state high council.
- Privatisation regulations need some amendments in order to speed up the process of selling off state-owned assets.
- Zeroual orders Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia to set up an independent committee to supervise parliamentary elections planned for the first half of 1997.
- Security forces search the High Casbah in Algiers.
- The government adopts a draft law on privatisation.
- Workers' union leader Abdelhaq Benhamouda says he is leaving his position at the union this year. He plans to form a political party.
- National Liberation Front leader Abdelkader Hajar says his party is ready for alliances with other parties ahead of the elections.
